We examine standard positive-definite corrections and two covariance estimators based on leave-one-out sample L-moments: the delete-one jackknife estimator and an estimator based on the H\'ajek projection. Both are positive semidefinite by construction. Simulation results show that the projection estimator generally has smaller estimation error and better numerical stability than the exact unbiased estimator. The jackknife estimator overestimates the variances of higher-order sample L-moments and has larger estimation error than the projection estimator. We also develop fast rank-prefix algorithms for the three covariance estimators considered. These algorithms substantially reduce computation time.

nominations.title: Unidentified prediction-risk rankings under spatial sampling with fixed inclusion probabilities
nominations.authors: Shinichiro Shirota
nominations.abstract: For Gaussian spatial prediction, we construct positive sampling mechanisms with identical observation laws and conditional site inclusion probabilities, yet opposite risk rankings for two fixed predictors. The construction selects two of four sites and allows independent Gaussian measurement error.

nominations.title: Functional-Specific Information Borrowing under Limited Overlap
nominations.authors: Shinichiro Shirota
nominations.abstract: Source observations can improve a target average without estimating the entire shared response accurately. We study this distinction in two independent observational samples whose treatment effects share a rough component and differ by a smoother discrepancy. For power-law treatment overlap known for the analysis, known design density, fixed positive Sobolev radii, and Gaussian noise, we derive matching minimax mean squared error bounds with three regimes. Two explicit source-information thresholds determine the onset of rate improvement and attainment of the source-known rate. A signed local correction explains the thresholds: source observations estimate only the part of the integration functional poorly recovered from the target sample. Direct likelihood lower bounds apply to all estimators. Existing joint reproducing-kernel recovery, which does not require propensity inputs, attains these rates, and standard bias-aware intervals are conditionally honest under the specified class. A supplementary zero-overlap result separates estimation error from residual identification uncertainty. Numerical results illustrate both gains and losses when the total number of participants is fixed. The intermediate rate depends on overlap geometry, while smoothness determines its two endpoints.

nominations.title: Observation-Specific Uncertainty Modeling for Latent-Variable Regression in High-Dimensional Analytical Data
nominations.authors: Carl Emil Eskildsen, Georgios Papadopoulos, Kevin A. Giraldo, Mauricio Barahona, Molly M. Stevens
nominations.abstract: Across many fields, including medical diagnostics, process monitoring, and quality control, decisions often rely on point predictions for single samples. Observation-specific uncertainty is needed to assess the risk of decision error when predictions are compared with thresholds. Latent-variable regression is widely used for such predictions, but observation-specific uncertainty remains difficult to estimate. Traditional methods assume unbiased predictions, attributing prediction uncertainty solely to variance. However, dimensionality reduction can introduce observation-specific bias, violating this assumption. We introduce a framework using Gaussian processes trained on latent scores and prediction errors to estimate observation-specific bias and error variance, separating systematic error from epistemic and aleatoric variance. In Raman measurements of a fructose-sucrose model system, estimated prediction-error distributions agreed with empirical distributions; bias correction reduced mean squared error, and decision limits incorporating bias and variance improved analyte detection over variance-only limits. An aqueous-solubility application using molecular descriptors demonstrated the framework's generalisation beyond spectroscopy.

nominations.title: Unifying Data-Adaptive Longitudinal Treatment-Effect Subgroup Discovery and Pretreatment Membership Prediction
nominations.authors: Pu Zhang, Yuheng Li, Jiakun Jiang
nominations.abstract: Precision medicine seeks to match patients with treatments from which they are most likely to benefit. A key step toward this goal is to learn treatment-effect heterogeneity from longitudinal study data. This requires discovering subgroups with distinct treatment-effect trajectories and predicting subgroup membership for new patients from pretreatment information. Existing methods do not fully unify these tasks. Covariate-informed membership models typically prespecify the subgroup number or covariance structure, whereas data-adaptive discovery methods often require prediction in a separate stage. We propose a data-adaptive semiparametric mixture-of-experts framework that unifies longitudinal treatment-effect subgroup discovery and pretreatment membership prediction. Subgroup-specific varying-coefficient functions characterize treatment-effect trajectories, while flexible covariance functions account for within-subject dependence. A covariate-dependent gating model links membership to pretreatment characteristics. A penalty on global component weights removes redundant subgroups, while separate gating coefficients allow patient-specific membership probabilities among retained subgroups. A blockwise generalized expectation--maximization algorithm estimates all model components under a single penalized observed-data objective. We establish consistent subgroup-number selection, convergence rates for the functional estimators, and asymptotic normality for the finite-dimensional parameters. Simulations show reliable subgroup-number selection and more accurate conditional membership prediction than a two-step procedure. Applications to the SANAD epilepsy study and the COMPETE migraine trial identify distinct temporal treatment-effect patterns.

nominations.title: Parametric inference for the average hazard approach in time-to-event analysis with sparse risk sets
nominations.authors: Zihan Qian, Lu Tian, Hajime Uno
nominations.abstract: The average hazard (AH) is a recently proposed model-free summary of an event-time distribution. Over a prespecified window $[0,\tau]$, it equals the cumulative incidence probability at $\tau$ divided by the restricted mean survival time at $\tau$ and can be interpreted as a person-time incidence rate that does not depend on the censoring distribution. The difference and ratio of AHs from two groups, DAH and RAH, are between-group contrasts on absolute and relative scales without requiring proportional hazards. Existing nonparametric inference for AH and its contrasts is based on the Kaplan--Meier estimator of the survival function, and can become unreliable when risk sets become sparse or exhausted near $\tau$, as may occur in stratified analyses. As a practical remedy, we investigate parametric AH inference using Weibull and generalized gamma models. We use maximum-likelihood estimators and corresponding confidence intervals for group-specific AHs, DAH and RAH in both unstratified and stratified analyses. Simulations show that under correct model specification, little bias and near-nominal coverage can be achieved in settings where nonparametric inference is inadequately supported by observed data. We illustrate the method using a randomized trial comparing neratinib plus capecitabine with lapatinib plus capecitabine in metastatic breast cancer. Parametric inference provides a practical complement to nonparametric AH analysis when sparse or exhausted risk sets make inference at clinically relevant truncation times less reliable.

nominations.title: A Semiparametric Model Approach to Data Integration under Missing Not at Random
nominations.authors: Danhyang Lee, Kosuke Morikawa, Jae Kwang Kim
nominations.abstract: Integrating probability and non-probability samples requires accounting for an unknown selection mechanism that may depend on the outcome. We develop a semiparametric approach in which an unspecified function captures covariate dependence and a scalar tilting parameter governs outcome dependence. Identification follows from an instrumental-variable exclusion restriction and conditional completeness; a zero tilt gives a restricted missing-at-random submodel. We profile out the covariate component and construct cross-fitted, Neyman-orthogonal estimating equations for both the tilting parameter and the finite population mean. The resulting orthogonalized mass-imputation estimator supports centered root-N inference under nuisance product-rate conditions. Its linearization variance accounts for the probability sampling design and estimation of the tilting parameter. Simulations illustrate the cost of flexibility under correct parametric specification, protection against misspecification of the covariate component, and the consequences of invalid instruments or a misspecified tilt. A further simulation using 50,000 national health-screening records finds smaller bias but higher root mean squared error than a parametric competitor under the baseline instrument set. The proposed estimator varies less across alternative instrument sets, although weak instruments and smoothing choices affect precision and interval coverage.

nominations.title: Co-sufficient weighting: leveraging sparsity for more powerful variable selection in the linear model
nominations.authors: Souhardya Sengupta, Lucas Janson
nominations.abstract: We show that for the problem of controlled variable selection in the Gaussian linear model, informative and p-value-independent weights (for weighted multiple testing) can be derived entirely from sufficient statistics and a belief in sparsity using only the data itself and no external quantitative side information. Using these weights, which we call \emph{co-sufficient weights} (CSW), in weighted versions of Holm's procedure and the Benjamini--Hochberg (BH) procedure results in substantially higher power than their unweighted analogues when the true coefficient vector is sparse, while retaining Holm's exact validity and BH's highly robust empirical validity regardless of sparsity. We demonstrate the superior performance of our proposed weighted methods compared to their unweighted analogues and other competing methods in a wide range of simulations and an application to HIV drug resistance.

nominations.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 3: expectation under a general distribution
nominations.authors: Nikola Bani\'c, Neven Elezovi\'c
nominations.abstract: For multinomial counts $X\sim\operatorname{Mult}(N;\mathbf p)$ on $n$ ordered bins and a reference law $\mathbf r$ we study the expectation of the reference-centered discrete total variation $d_{\mathbf r}(X)=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}|(X_{j+1}-Nr_{j+1})-(X_j-Nr_j)|$, the natural extension of the comb-test statistic to a non-uniform null. For a non-uniform null the raw total variation of the counts carries a deterministic staircase of order $N$ that no centering of the statistic removes; the counts are therefore centered at the reference law, and under the null ($\mathbf p=\mathbf r$) the statistic is the matched $d_{\mathbf p}$. Exact finite-sample expectations are obtained by conditioning on the total mass in each adjacent pair, which reduces every edge to a translated binomial absolute-deviation problem. For fixed $n\ge3$ and a sampling law bounded away from the boundary of the simplex, the matched statistic admits a three-term asymptotic expansion in powers of $1/N$ whose coefficients are explicit continuous periodic functions of $N(p_{j+1}-p_j)$ (a generalized, non-Poincar\'e asymptotic expansion), obtained by a weighted local Edgeworth estimate and a corner Euler--Maclaurin summation; all half-integer orders vanish by parity. Each correction separates into a smooth Edgeworth part and an oscillatory lattice part, the latter an Edgeworth perturbation of one formal Euler--Maclaurin series of a Gaussian lattice sum. Under a sampling law $\mathbf p\neq\mathbf r$ the leading expectation is the folded-normal profile implied by the central limit theorem; under local alternatives we identify the $O(1)$ correction (a skewness term, plus a variance-gradient term for Pitman alternatives), and fixed alternatives give a law-of-large-numbers limit, the $\ell_1$ distance between the adjacent-gradient profiles of $\mathbf p$ and $\mathbf r$, on which threshold tests are consistent.

nominations.title: Dimension Changes the Scale-Signal Channel in Nearest-Neighbor Two-Sample Testing
nominations.authors: Hao Chen
nominations.abstract: Nearest-neighbor two-sample tests are often analyzed with dimension fixed. We study the power of the generalized edge-count test on a directed 1-nearest-neighbor graph. This statistic combines a weighted sum and a difference of the two within-sample edge counts. For balanced isotropic Gaussian samples with $d/\log N\to\gamma>0$, we derive the connection probabilities under local location and scale alternatives. Under location alternatives, the two counts have equal mean shifts, which cancel in their difference. Under scale alternatives, the two counts instead have mean shifts of opposite signs. We also derive the growth rate of the null expectation $\mathbb{E}_0C_3$, where $C_3$ counts pairs of directed edges sharing exactly one vertex. On an explicit range of $\gamma$, we establish local-power limits strictly above the test level for scale alternatives in the difference component at the scale $|\varepsilon_N|\asymp (\mathbb{E}_0C_3)^{1/2}/(Nd)$. Here $\mathbb{E}_0C_3$ gives the variance order of the difference count under these local alternatives. At this scale, the standardized drift of the weighted sum vanishes. When $d=1$, the weighted component instead detects local Gaussian scale alternatives while the difference component has no limiting drift. Thus dimension changes both the magnitude of a detectable scale difference and the component of the test that detects it.

nominations.title: Simultaneous inference for additive regression
nominations.authors: Donghyun Kim, Changwon Choi
nominations.abstract: This paper develops methods for simultaneous inference on component functions in additive models. We first propose bias-corrected smooth backfitting estimators inspired by least squares linear regression and establish their asymptotic properties. We then show that the distributions of the uniform errors of these estimators converge to a Gumbel-type distribution. Based on this distributional approximation, we construct simultaneous confidence bands and develop a practical residual-based procedure for testing the additive components. Simulation studies and empirical data analyses demonstrate that the proposed estimators reduce bias and improve estimation accuracy compared with several existing estimators. Moreover, the empirical coverage probabilities of the proposed simultaneous confidence bands are found to be comparable to those of their oracle counterparts.

nominations.title: Bethe Hessian Recovery through the Kesten-Stigum Regime
nominations.authors: Dingding Dong, Theo McKenzie
nominations.abstract: We show that outlier eigenvectors of the Bethe Hessian achieve weak recovery in the stochastic block model down to the Kesten-Stigum threshold, for every fixed common expected degree $d>1$. This extends previous recovery guarantees, which required $d$ to be sufficiently large. This threshold is information-theoretically optimal for the symmetric two-community model and is conjectured to mark the limit of efficient recovery in broader symmetric models. Our result matches the recovery guarantees of non-backtracking spectral methods while using Hermitian $n\times n$ matrices. To do this, we identify recursive formulas for the negative outlier eigenvalues and show that their eigenspaces have nonvanishing overlap with the corresponding planted eigenspaces. The proof constructs approximate eigenvectors from the planted labels on the limiting Poisson tree, with weights given by its Green's function, and transfers these approximations to the finite graph.

nominations.title: Improved estimation of differential entropy of a multivariate Gaussian distribution
nominations.authors: Somnath Mondal, Lakshmi Kanta Patra
nominations.abstract: We consider estimation of entropy of a multivariate variate normal distribution with unknown mean vector and unknown covariance matrix. Using a decision-theoretic approach, we study the problem under a general location-invariant loss function that is strictly convex and minimized at zero. We first characterize the class of affine equivariant estimators and obtain the best affine equivariant estimator. We further show that the best affine equivariant estimator is inadmissible under the general loss. Exploiting information in the sample mean, we derive Stein-type improved estimators, including an extension to the case of a mean matrix. Under the linex loss, we obtain a smooth Brewster--Zidek-type estimator that dominates the best affine equivariant estimator, and we show that this estimator is generalized Bayes under a suitable non-informative prior.

nominations.title: On Statistical-Computational Gaps in Graph Combinatorial Testing Problems
nominations.authors: Ikjun Choi, Pratik Patil, Alessandro Rinaldo
nominations.abstract: We study high-dimensional graph combinatorial hypothesis testing problems in which a signal is supported on the edge set of an unknown subgraph drawn from a class invariant under vertex relabeling. For Gaussian observations, we characterize sharp statistical and computational thresholds (at polynomial order) for the signal magnitude required for strong detection across various combinatorial graph alternatives. Our analysis is based on bounding the second moments of the full and low-degree likelihood ratios in terms of the overlap of two independent latent structures and comparing the resulting lower bounds with scan, average, and coordinatewise maximum tests. Under an appropriate low-degree conjecture for computational hardness, we obtain planted-clique thresholds matching those known for Gaussian submatrix detection and identify new statistical-computational gaps for multiple planted cliques and hypercliques, thick cycles and thick paths. We also establish a novel transfer principle across natural exponential family observation models: matching the one-coordinate chi-square divergence preserves full likelihood-ratio second moments exactly and makes low-degree second moments equivalent up to constant factors under a degree condition. Under local regularity, we obtain corresponding testing upper bounds in terms of an effective signal strength. When these upper and lower bounds match, they yield universal threshold scales in the local alternative regime. As a consequence, statistical-computational gaps for planted-clique detection in Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi settings can be deduced from the Gaussian model.

nominations.title: Variance-adaptive Chernoff bounds: nonasymptotically valid, asymptotically sharp confidence sets for unbounded means
nominations.authors: Aaditya Ramdas, Diego Martinez-Taboada
nominations.abstract: Consider the classical statistical problem of sub-Gaussian mean estimation under martingale dependence: given $n$ observations with conditional mean $\mu$ and a known conditional sub-Gaussian proxy $s>0$, we seek a nonasymptotically valid confidence interval for $\mu$. The usual Chernoff interval has half-width $s\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)/n}$; it neither adapts to the actual standard deviation $\sigma\le s$ nor attains the Gaussian quantile $z_{1-\alpha/2}$. We construct an analytically closed-form nonasymptotically-valid interval under martingale dependence whose endpoints, at every iid law with $\sigma > 0$, agree almost surely to first order with $\bar X_n\pm\sigma z_{1-\alpha/2}/\sqrt n$. The two new building blocks are a sub-Gaussian exponential supermartingale with an \emph{empirical} quadratic variance and a cubic correction term, and a sub-Gaussian continuation supermartingale, the former delivering variance adaptivity ("Empirical-Bernstein'' for unbounded data), the latter also providing the Gaussian quantile ("Empirical-Berry-Esseen'' for unbounded data). The same constructions yield a closed-form time-uniform confidence sequence with asymptotically unimprovable half-width $\sigma\sqrt{2\log\log n/n}$. We also give closed-form multivariate ellipsoids with the true-covariance chi-square limit, and extend the scalar Gaussian and LIL constructions to handle heavy-tailed settings where one only knows a bound on any absolute central moment of order greater than two. Experiments show substantial width reductions when the true variance is smaller than the implied variance bound, at small loss in the boundary cases. The surprising (to us) takeaway message is: given any more than two moments, one can construct fully data dependent nonasymptotic confidence sets for the mean that are asymptotically efficient.

nominations.title: Weak Identification in Bunching Designs: Rare Events and Counterfactual Uncertainty
nominations.authors: Kun Huang
nominations.abstract: We study shrinking tax kinks when the counterfactual density is locally H\"older continuous and may be accompanied by a known background atom at the threshold. Small policy incentives create two distinct obstacles: few behavioral bunchers and an unobserved relocation interval. For the complete observed distribution, we establish matching minimax bounds for elasticity estimation and honest confidence-set diameter. With kink size $d$, background mass $\gamma$, and smoothness $0<s\leq1$, the rate is $\min\{1,\sqrt{(\gamma+d)/(nd^2)}+d^s\}$. The stochastic component has a rare-event scale when the background mass is of the kink order or smaller and a conventional weak-signal scale when it remains positive. The extrapolation component follows from observationally equivalent counterfactual densities, rather than sampling error. We derive normal and Poisson limits for a conventional bunching ratio, show a coverage failure of its Wald interval, and give finite-sample confidence sets by exact binomial inversion with a deterministic smoothness allowance. The procedure estimates the counterfactual density from an unaffected bin and covers the entire population identified set uniformly, including zero policy incentives. A likelihood-ratio calculation establishes a finite-parameter Poisson limit for a smooth, known counterfactual submodel. Structural Monte Carlo experiments document both coverage protection and its cost in set length. The results apply to the stated exact-atom observation model; general rounding and optimization frictions require additional assumptions.

nominations.title: Convolution Skew-$t$ Distributions
nominations.authors: Xinxian Chen, Peter Reinhard Hansen, Chen Tong
nominations.abstract: We introduce the convolution skew-$t$ (CST) distribution, which combines independent standardized skew-$t$ subvectors through a general loading matrix to accommodate heterogeneous tails, directional asymmetry, and non-elliptical dependence. We establish identification and develop likelihood inference using analytical scores and a one-dimensional reduction of Fisher information. For the finite-variance model, we prove consistency and asymptotic normality of maximum likelihood and characterize the consequences of imposing false symmetry. A raw representation extends the family to all positive tail indices. Simulations assess finite-sample performance, and a realized-volatility application illustrates the empirical value of allowing tail thickness and asymmetry to vary across latent subvectors.

nominations.title: The Double Diagonal Estimator: Reducing Bias in Two-Sided Marketplace Experiments
nominations.authors: Saanvi Chawla, Vasilis Syrgkanis
nominations.abstract: Interference between participants in two-sided marketplace experiments can severely bias conventional A/B tests. While two-sided randomization (TSR), which randomizes both supply and demand, enables estimators that mitigate this bias, existing analyses offer limited guidance on which estimator to prefer for the balanced market conditions common in practice, as they largely focus on extreme supply- or demand-constrained regimes. We introduce the Double Diagonal (DD) estimator, a novel method for interference-robust treatment effect estimation. The DD estimator contrasts the outcomes of treated-treated and control-control pairs and uses the off-diagonal interactions (treated-control and control-treated) to correct for interference-induced bias. We provide the first theoretical comparison between the DD and the standard naive TSR (TSRN) estimator under a simplifying mean-field market model, proving two key results: (i) DD's bias is strictly smaller than the standard estimator's below a critical threshold of the outside-option parameter; in particular, DD's bias is smaller whenever the outside option is at most twice as attractive as platform options; and (ii) the two estimators exhibit biases in opposite directions, with DD underestimating and the standard estimator overestimating the true effect, respectively. Extensive numerical experiments in realistic market settings--spanning heterogeneous treatment effects, supply-demand imbalances, and varied market structures--corroborate our theoretical findings. Across a wide range of configurations, the DD estimator demonstrates the lowest bias, establishing it as a robust and often superior choice for reliable experimentation in two-sided marketplaces.

nominations.title: Identification through Heteroskedasticity in One Lemma: Partial Identification, an Eigenvalue Construction, and a Caution on Rank Tests
nominations.authors: George Milunovich
nominations.abstract: This teaching note unifies known results on identification through heteroskedasticity, under volatility regimes, GARCH, stochastic volatility and covariate-driven variances, in one lemma with a short linear-algebra proof. A shock is identified up to sign and labelling if and only if no other shock shares its variance path, and shocks that share a path are identified up to a rotation. The rows of the structural coefficient matrix solve one generalised eigenvalue problem that nests Rigobon's (2003) two-regime solution. Rank tests on second moments of the errors count at most linearly independent centred variance paths, not identified shocks. A simulation illustrates each point.

nominations.title: xtlp: A new Stata command for panel local projection
nominations.authors: Shu Shen, Ziwei Mei, Liugang Sheng, Zhentao Shi
nominations.abstract: Panel local projection (LP) estimated with fixed effects (FEs) is widely used to evaluate the dynamic effects of economic shocks across countries or regions. However, FE estimation of panel LP models is subject to Nickell bias arising from the predictive structure of LP specifications, even when lagged dependent variables are not included in the regressors. This bias invalidates standard inference based on conventional t-statistics. We introduce xtlp, a new Stata command that implements panel LP with split-panel jackknife (SPJ) bias correction. It removes the Nickell bias and restores the validity of standard statistical inference. The command accommodates a broad range of specifications, including different transformations of the dependent variable, additional control variables, and flexible variance estimators. We illustrate xtlp through empirical applications that examine the effects of financial crises on output.

nominations.title: Covariance Identification from Regression Residuals
nominations.authors: Yanping Chen
nominations.abstract: Regression residuals are projections of the errors, not observations of them. This paper characterizes what residuals identify about the error covariance. Residualization acts on the covariance through a known linear map, and under an unrestricted covariance model the directions it destroys are exactly those generated by the column space of the regressors. A linear covariance functional is identified if and only if it does not load on these lost directions, and restricting the covariance model, for instance to diagonal or clustered form, shrinks them. The central result separates projection loss from moment-selection loss: projecting the residual covariance onto the maintained covariance structure loses no identifying information, so cross-cluster, long-lag, and long-distance residual products add no identifying directions. They can still improve conditioning, since restricting to the aligned moments squares the condition number. This equivalence relies on the orthogonal-projection geometry of OLS, and generally fails for non-orthogonal transformation. Quadratic statistics in the outcome that are free of the regression coefficients additionally identify the covariance between the fitted and residual components, but not the covariance within the span of the regressors. Because the OLS sandwich variance depends only on that block, it is not identified by any such statistic under an unrestricted covariance model; robust variance estimation draws its identification from maintained restrictions on the covariance structure.

nominations.title: Evaluating Maternity Leave Reforms When RD Fails
nominations.authors: Clara von Bismarck-Osten, Andrei Zeleneev
nominations.abstract: This paper documents that expansions of UK maternity pay in the 2000s improved children's test scores while reducing maternal employment. Extending job protection alone generated similar employment effects but no detectable impact on children. None of these effects are recoverable with a conventional regression discontinuity (RD) design because eligibility is only imperfectly captured by the available data. We explain why existing corrections for measurement error in RD are not well suited and propose a simple imputation-based solution. The approach preserves RD's main advantages, nonparametric identification and transparency, and remains valid even when measurement error has economic content.

nominations.title: Zero Crossings on the Accuracy-Smoothness Frontier: Maximal Monotone and Minimal Inflection Non Stationary Predictors
nominations.authors: Marc Wildi
nominations.abstract: The Smooth Sign Accuracy (SSA) framework resolves the smoothness--accuracy dilemma for stationary predictors by balancing mean squared error (MSE) against the frequency of sign changes. We generalize it to non-stationary integrated processes (I-SSA), deriving MSE-optimal predictors constrained by the expected duration between turning points (I(1)) or inflection points (I(2)). The resulting maximal-monotone and minimal-inflection predictors, filters, and smoothers customize classic benchmarks along a new efficient Accuracy--Smoothness (AS) frontier. Tracking the identity (the original data) along this frontier defines the \emph{I-SSA trend}, a novel smoothing concept that, unlike classical filters, imposes no artificial structure on the data-generating process and is directly interpretable through explicit control of turning- or inflection-point frequency. The optimization is a quadratically constrained quadratic program (QCQP) that reduces to a Generalized Trust Region Subproblem (GTRS) with hidden convexity. On its feasible, invertible region the problem is convex with a well-defined global optimum, and an exact closed-form expression delivers the efficient AS frontier. Under fairly general assumptions, finite-sample solutions converge to an asymptotic I-SSA predictor, devoid of integration boundary perturbations. The framework unifies mean squared error on non-stationary levels, and sign accuracy, zero-crossing frequency, and target correlation on stationary differences.

nominations.title: Valid GMM Inference with Non-parametrically Generated Discrete Type
nominations.authors: Taegyu Yang
nominations.abstract: The recent progress in machine learning and classification methods has enabled researchers to predict economic discrete attributes that are not observed in standard datasets. These range from missing demographics, such as ethnicity and poverty status, to economic categories, such as innovative firms, metropolitan areas, occupational groups, binary treatment status, and counterfactual status. Although the plug-in procedure is widely used in empirical applications, nonparametric first-stage estimation recovering the labels can introduce regularization bias because of its slow convergence rate. Even if the double/debiased machine learning approach provides a way to correct the regularization bias, the according bias-correction term is not well defined in our problem, because even a small first-stage error can change the type discontinuously. To address this problem, we smooth the discontinuous type indicators using a smooth kernel function and a shrinking tuning parameter $b$. We then construct a well-defined Neyman-orthogonal score and define the appropriate debiased estimator. We show that this debiased estimator satisfies $\sqrt{Nb}$-consistency and asymptotic normality under regularity conditions. The slower $\sqrt{Nb}$ convergence rate is the cost of correcting the regularization bias when the nonparametric first-stage learner enters the moment function through discontinuous functions.

nominations.title: A small HER2 reader for routine H&E slides: real-world deployment
nominations.authors: Thang Tran (CloudKites AI Lab, New South Wales, Australia), Lan Dang (Monash Business School, Monash University, Victoria, Australia)
nominations.abstract: HER2 status decides who receives HER2-targeted therapy. Pathologists score HER2 protein by immunohistochemistry (IHC); equivocal IHC 2+ tumours, their hardest calls, wait for in situ hybridisation (ISH). We built a HER2 reader for routine H&E slides, owned end to end, as a baseline for pathologists. A 22M-parameter ViT-S/16 tile encoder was trained on public TCGA slides by self-supervision, distillation from H-optimus-0 and two rounds of JEPA refinement; five cross-validated attention-based slide classifiers average their probabilities; and an operating point is fixed on training data. Compared under one paired ten-seed protocol, readers on our encoder rank first of 7 on external validation from TCGA-BRCA to Yale-HER2 (AUC 0.812), level with readers on encoders 4 and 50 times larger. We also rebuilt PathBench's encoder benchmark on public cohorts; our replica reproduces its published order of reference encoders, and under it our encoder ranks first of 7 on TCGA-BRCA (0.689) and sits level with H-optimus-0 and Phikon on Yale-HER2 (0.897). On three external hospitals our deployed reader reaches AUC 0.82 on Yale-HER2 (about 0.81 with training slides balanced for tissue size), 0.75 on HEROHE and 0.63 on BCNB biopsies, and among HEROHE's 85 IHC 2+ cases it ranks ISH-amplified above non-amplified tumours at 0.76, best among our TCGA-trained readers. Per-laboratory score normalisation and a laboratory's own slides improve it further on a new site. Without a GPU our reader needs 5-6 s per slide. It serves as a research-use pre-read in a pathology platform, where it proposes a probability and a call beside IHC and helps prioritise ISH for equivocal cases. Weights, per-slide predictions and the data behind every figure are public at https://huggingface.co/cloudkites/her2-reader.

nominations.title: Intervention-Conditioned Counterfactual Human Digital Twin Generator
nominations.authors: Saeed Farzi, Sofia Michopoulou, Christopher Kipps, Rahman Attar
nominations.abstract: Chronic diseases evolve through long, heterogeneous trajectories shaped by interacting mediators, confounders, and treatment histories. Estimating long-term patient trajectories under alternative interventions is essential for in silico clinical trial design. However, most existing models overlook irregular visit intervals and cross-mediator dependencies, both of which are crucial for reliable long-term longitudinal prediction. Moreover, these models typically focus on outcome prediction rather than generating complete patient-state trajectories. To address these challenges, we propose CHDT, an intervention-conditioned Human Digital Twin generator under standard identification assumptions for multimodal longitudinal trajectory estimation. Its main empirical advantage arises from explicit modeling of irregular visit intervals, while cross-mediator refinement provides additional gains in selected intervention-conditioned settings. Across real-world ADNI and simulator-generated ALPACA cohorts, CHDT shows improved long-horizon patient-state fidelity relative to competing baselines. Ablation results indicate that irregular-time conditioning provides the primary empirical gain, and cross-mediator refinement provides additional improvements.

nominations.title: Recycle only when you have to!
nominations.authors: Lorenz Vaitl, Ivan Tanasijevic, Arian Rokkum Jamasb, L. Santiago Mille-Fragoso, Pan Kessel
nominations.abstract: AlphaFold 3-like models (e.g., Boltz, Protenix, etc.) have pushed the frontier of protein binder design. This architecture is used both for the generation of binder candidates (e.g., by hallucination or converting these models into backbone or full atom generative models) as well as for the screening of these candidates for valid binders. In this paper, we start from the observation that AlphaFold 3's confidence metrics (ipSAE, ipTM) as well as structural consistency metrics can be predicted directly from the trunk even at early recycling. Because our proposed predictor is cheap, differentiable, and available at every cycle, it can be used in two distinct ways: as a decision signal to wisely spend the recycling budget for screening and as an objective for hallucination-based design. We show that both applications lead to increased performance at significantly reduced computational cost.

nominations.title: Physics-Grounded Simulation Enables Zero-Shot Molecular and Reaction Analysis in Scanning Tunneling Microscopy
nominations.authors: Yuanqin He, Zhiyu Wang, Yang Bao, Tao Lin, Hai Bi
nominations.abstract: Quantitative identification of molecular products and reaction pathways from scanning tunneling microscopy images is difficult when labeled images are unavailable for a new chemical system. We develop a simulation-assisted framework for zero-shot analysis that requires only precursor information for a new target system, with no experimental images or annotations from that system used during model training. The framework couples two functional components: NanoSim generates physics-grounded synthetic images from predicted reaction products and sampled surface scenes, while NanoAnalysis translates molecular detections into product populations, spatial arrangements, and mechanistic interpretations. Applied to a representative on-surface reaction, the detector achieves a micro-averaged F1 score of 0.92 on experimental images. Analysis of the detected molecules reveals annealing-dependent population changes and reaction-site preferences consistent with experimental observations. Beyond this capability, its modular organization allows heterogeneous data from other systems to be used to improve each component independently, providing a scalable route for continued generalization.

nominations.title: GraphTFactor: A graph-based approach for proteins transcription factor prediction
nominations.authors: Domenico Amato, Salvatore Calderaro, Giosu\`e Lo Bosco, Riccardo Rizzo, Filippo Vella
nominations.abstract: Transcription factors (TFs) play an important role in regulating gene expression, making their identification a fundamental task in computational biology. In this work, we propose GraphTFactor, a novel end-to-end framework that models protein sequences as graphs and directly classifies transcription factors. By encoding sequences into graph structures, the proposed approach naturally handles variable-length inputs while preserving relevant relational information, without imposing length constraints. Experimental results show that GraphTFactor outperforms state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of graph-based representations for TF prediction while providing interpretable insights into the sequence regions contributing to the model's predictions. To support reproducibility and practical adoption, we release an open-source software package and an interactive web application that let users easily perform TF prediction on custom sequences.

nominations.title: Temporal and spatial couplings in the dynamics of human walking and running
nominations.authors: Mustafa Mert Ankarali
nominations.abstract: Rhythmic behaviours such as walking and running are commonly modelled as dynamical systems around a stable limit cycle. To keep such models tractable, it is usually assumed that each step depends only on the previous one, that the limit cycle is fixed, and that the sagittal and frontal planes can be studied separately. Here, we test these assumptions in seven public datasets of human gait (71 participants), including 16 people who both walked and ran. We fit linear step-to-step maps and validate them by cross-validation, holding out more data where more data exist. At first sight, gait has memory: the state two steps back lowers the prediction error by up to 29\%. Yet most of this temporal coupling vanishes once the operating point may drift slowly and measurement noise is modelled; gait remains limit-cycle-like, around an operating point that moves. Running keeps more memory than walking in the same people. Spatial coupling between the planes is present in most participants, mainly from sagittal to frontal, but weak. This supports planar models of healthy gait, while a repeatable, task-dependent coupling index may serve as a measure of gait quality. The simple models are wrong, but useful enough.

nominations.title: Co$^2$ODE: Conditionally Coarse-Grained Model Discovery for Rewiring in Biochemical Networks
nominations.authors: Theodore de Pomereu, Fabian Fr\"ohlich
nominations.abstract: Biochemical networks propagate the signals that regulate cellular behaviour, and which routes carry them depends on cellular context: a shift in context rewires the network's effective dynamics. Mechanistic simulators are misspecified here because the effective dynamics emerge from an interaction structure that is only partially known. Model discovery instead learns the dynamics from data, but sparse, correlated measurements poorly identify a full network model. What matters is narrower: the portion the context rewires. We introduce conditionally coarse-grained ODEs (Co$^2$ODE), which model that portion as a sparse neural or symbolic ODE: a conditional mask selects the markers carrying the rewiring, and a variational autoencoder compresses the remaining markers into a learnt closure term. On single-cell phosphoproteomic data spanning 30 cancer-relevant overexpressions, Co$^2$ODE compresses a 30-marker panel into a 10-dimensional state while matching the predictive accuracy of a neural ODE fit to the full panel. The closure absorbs what the mask drops, hence the accuracy is insensitive to which markers are kept. Adding a prior score to the loss shifts the selected markers at no cost in fit, indicating the data are not interventional enough to identify the underlying biology.

nominations.title: Joint Estimation and Network Configuration in Multi-Agent Systems
nominations.authors: Mohammadreza Barzegaran, Hamid Jafarkhani
nominations.abstract: Distributed consensus-based sensing enables a multi-agent system to collaboratively estimate an unknown state by combining local measurements with information received from neighboring agents. In practice, however, the communication network, transmission delays, and finite-rate communication directly affect the disagreement among agents. On the other hand, agreement among agents does not ensure accuracy, particularly when sensors have different measurement uncertainties. We develop a sampled consensus-plus-innovations framework under realistic wireless network constraints that jointly accounts for inter-agent disagreement and estimation inaccuracy. We derive a computable upper bound on the worst-case steady-state estimation error that captures consensus disagreement due to the communication graph, quantization error, and transmission delay, together with estimation inaccuracy, which accounts for measurement uncertainty against the true state. We then use this bound as a network design objective and propose a semi-distributed auction-based algorithm that jointly modifies the communication graph and link-rate allocation. The proposed method preserves connectivity, converges in finite time to a locally auction-stable network configuration, and reduces the bound on the estimation error at every accepted change. The proposed method has been evaluated on various test cases, and the results show that it reduces the estimation error while maintaining fewer links and allocating moderate link rates in a short time.

nominations.title: Maxwell-Consistent 3-D Magnetic Field Camera using Scalar-Potential-Based Reconstruction
nominations.authors: Paul J\"ur{\ss}, Marija Boberg, Philip Suskin, Tobias Knopp, Fynn Foerger
nominations.abstract: Various applications require accurate 3-D characterization of magnetic fields with high spatial and temporal resolution. Building on our previously introduced spherical magnetic field camera employing 86 three-axis Hall sensors arranged on a spherical surface, we present a novel magnetic-field reconstruction approach based on the magnetic scalar potential and its spherical harmonic expansion. Unlike the previous reconstruction method that expands each vector component separately, our scalar-potential-based formulation is inherently consistent with Maxwell's equations for source-free fields by design, yielding curl-free and divergence-free field models. Using a simulated magnetic gradient field generated by two permanent magnets, we demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher reconstruction accuracy, improved robustness to sensor noise and failure, and substantially reduced non-physical divergence and curl compared to the component-wise baseline. Furthermore, the scalar-potential approach attains superior performance with fewer coefficients, indicating a more efficient use of measurement data allowing higher-degree polynomial representations.

nominations.title: Automated Optimization of Patient-Specific Electro-Anatomical Models Fitted to Cochlear Implant SCINSEV
nominations.authors: Minh Q. Vu, Erin L. Bratu, Jack H. Noble
nominations.abstract: Purpose: Patient-specific electro-anatomical models (EAMs) of the implanted cochlea are crucial for auditory nerve fiber simulation in cochlear implant (CI) programming and neural health estimation. Fitting an EAM to the stimulation current induced non-stimulating electrode voltage (SCINSEV) currently requires manual expert adjustment or exhaustive search over precomputed forward solutions, neither of which scales to routine clinical use. We present an automated optimization pipeline that fits patient specific EAMs in minutes. Methods: Four compartment tissue label maps (perilymph, soft tissue, modiolus, and bone) derived from postoperative CT were used to construct a finite difference forward model, fitted to the measured SCINSEV by Gaussian process Bayesian optimization. Three reductions cut fitting cost: a coarsened grid with trilinear injection and readout at sub-voxel contact positions; solving half the stimulating contacts and completing three quarters of the matrix by reciprocity; and a Jacobian-based identifiability analysis reducing four resistivities to two. Each reduction was validated separately against the measurement's reciprocity residual and the reproducibility of the fit. Results: Across 43 implanted ears, fitting took a median of 2.6 minutes per ear. Median SCINSEV RMSE on the reduced-resolution objective was 0.069 mV, against 0.084 mV for grid search at a matched evaluation budget. Against an exhaustive full-resolution grid search requiring a median of 9.1 hours per ear, the pipeline reached statistically indistinguishable fitting error roughly 210x faster. Conclusion: Patient-specific cochlear EAM fitting can be performed at clinically practical timescales without expert supervision, removing a major computational barrier to patient-specific cochlear implant programming and cochlear simulation.

nominations.title: Prediction-Induced Sparsity for Tracked FMCW Radar: A Track-Conditioned Event-Gap FPGA Architecture
nominations.authors: Huy Trinh
nominations.abstract: Tracked FMCW radar already carries a prediction of the next target state, yet the downstream digital hardware is commonly provisioned for a fixed spectral search. We present prediction-induced sparsity (PIS), a tracked-mode architecture that uses the prior before event formation and hardware scheduling. The predicted beat is derotated to an innovation-centred coordinate, while tracker covariance is propagated to a bounded residual support K. Sparse level-crossing packets are then executed by an exact event-gap resonator engine with a shared complex processing element and K-dependent state/coefficient memory. On a public FMCW dataset, causal prior-only con- ditioning reduces event records by 33.1% on average, and the representative fixed-point stream is bit-exact in RTL. And on an Artix-7 implementation, reducing physical support from 129 to 23 states lowers LUT and BRAM use by 65.0% and 88.1%, respectively, and reduces measured VCCINT power by 19.9% at matched throughput. The results show how tracking uncertainty can become a hardware-capacity implication for future adaptive radar accelerators.

nominations.title: Downlink MU-MIMO for LEO Direct-to-Device: Feasibility, Architecture, and Implementation
nominations.authors: Bikshapathi Gouda, Neng Wang, Masoud Sajadieh, Meghna Agrawal
nominations.abstract: Direct-to-device connectivity from low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites is commercially available, but its throughput is limited by the satellite antenna size and by payloads that separate users only by beams and frequency reuse. This article shows that a single LEO satellite with a meter-scale array can serve hundreds of users on the same time-frequency resource through multi-user multiple-input multiple-output precoding. The number of users it can separate with a single stream each, i.e., its spatial degrees of freedom (DoF), follows from the aperture in wavelengths, the orbit altitude, and the minimum elevation angle. With minimum mean-square error (MMSE) precoding, the throughput of these users grows with the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), whereas maximum-ratio transmission becomes interference-limited. The precoder can be computed from the user positions and the satellite ephemeris and attitude, with a throughput loss of less than 0.5\% at 20~dB SNR compared with perfect channel knowledge under the 3GPP non-terrestrial channel models. The DoF also set the number of digital chains of a hybrid payload, and the functional split among satellites and ground trades inter-satellite-link and feeder-link load against on-board processing. As the satellite moves, the precoder can be updated from the known geometry every radio frame, i.e., 10~ms, while the computationally intensive user pairing can be kept for a few seconds with a throughput loss below 1\%. Finally, we keep the cell-specific signals on fixed beams while precoding the user data jointly across all cells of the satellite. For a $50\times50$ array at 600~km and a minimum elevation angle of $60^\circ$, one satellite serves 410 users at 6.1~bps/Hz on average, more than four times the throughput of fixed beams with four-color frequency reuse.

nominations.title: Pinching Antennas for ISAC: Waveguide Architectures, Solutions, and Future Directions
nominations.authors: Qian Gao, Ruikang Zhong
nominations.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is a core design principle for sixth-generation (6G) wireless systems, yet fixed antenna geometry limits its performance. Pinching antenna systems (PASS) guide electromagnetic waves along dielectric waveguides and radiate them through position-adaptive antennas, allowing communication links and sensing observations to benefit from spatial reconfiguration. This article reviews PASS-enabled ISAC through single-waveguide, multi-waveguide, and segmented-waveguide architectures, comparing their feed structures, spatial degrees of freedom, operating protocols, and uplink/downlink support. We organize solution pathways around physics-consistent modeling, joint spatial-signal optimization, dynamic channel acquisition, and stable real-time control. A segmented waveguide-enabled pinching-antenna array (SWAN) case study demonstrates joint segment selection, antenna po?sitioning, and transmit beamforming using segment-hysteresis reinforcement learning. The results illustrate how waveguide loss and per-segment aperture gain create communication-sensing tradeoffs. We conclude with research directions in joint transmit?receive operation, measurement-calibrated digital twins, and trustworthy control.

nominations.title: Fluid Antenna Systems for ISAC Design: A Survey
nominations.authors: Yueling Zhao, Ping Yang, Hong Niu, Shuaixin Yang, Yue Xiao, Gang Wu, Merouane Debbah, Ertugrul Basar
nominations.abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FAS) introduce dynamic positional degrees of freedom (DoFs), extending the spatial domain from a static and discrete resource to a quasi-continuous and reconfigurable design space. This spatial flexibility provides an effective means of alleviating the geometric rigidity and functional conflicts that constrain integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Against this backdrop, we provide a comprehensive overview of FAS-enabled ISAC, tracing the evolution from theoretical performance limits to practical transceiver architectures. To illustrate the surveyed design evolution, we further propose the fluid antenna multi-mode modulation (FA-MM) framework as a representative case study of multidimensional physical-layer design for FAS-ISAC. Finally, several open challenges are discussed, with emphasis on predictive sensing, adaptive coordination, and secure spatial-state management in future FAS-ISAC systems.

nominations.title: PolarFlow: Spectral Geometric Flow Matching for Directed Graph Generation via Polar Decomposition
nominations.authors: Yanan Zhao, Feng Ji, Alba Carballo-Castro, Jingyang Dai, Antonio Ortega, Pascal Frossard, Wee Peng Tay
nominations.abstract: Directed graphs model asymmetric relationships in biology, transportation, social networks, and electronic design automation. Recent discrete diffusion and flow-matching methods generate directed graphs effectively, but their edge-wise categorical formulations require dense predictions over all ordered node pairs and repeated categorical updates during generation. This motivates a fundamental question: can comparable generative quality be achieved through a more computationally efficient formulation that better exploits the structure of directed adjacency matrices? Existing benchmarks also cover limited network structures, restricting comprehensive evaluation. We introduce PolarFlow, a continuous geometric flow-matching framework based on polar decomposition and truncated spectral coordinates. Its representation comprises four coupled components: a Stiefel frame and rotation angles encoding the orthogonal factor, and a second Stiefel frame and nonnegative eigenvalues characterizing the positive-semidefinite factor. PolarFlow learns a joint velocity field along geometry-aware conditional paths on this product space, reconstructs a continuous adjacency-score matrix, and discretizes it into a binary directed graph. By replacing discrete edge-wise generation with joint continuous transport, PolarFlow improves computational efficiency while retaining global adjacency structure. To broaden evaluation, we introduce complementary Circuit and Twitter benchmarks spanning engineered functional and naturally evolved social networks. Across synthetic and real-world datasets, PolarFlow achieves generative quality comparable to competitive discrete methods while substantially reducing training and sampling time.

nominations.title: GNSS Receiver Operating Point Comparison Between Vector and Scalar Tracking Under High-Dynamics
nominations.authors: J. Ferm\'in Llorente, Ernesto M. L\'opez, Javier A. Smidt, Pedro A. Roncagliolo
nominations.abstract: This paper presents a measurement noise adaptation mechanism for Kalman filter-based carrier tracking in a navigation-aided GNSS receiver designed for launch-vehicle applications. The tracking loop is tuned for 20\,g acceleration steps, which requires a wide bandwidth that makes the loop vulnerable to noise-driven pull-out at low carrier-to-noise density ratios. To resolve this tradeoff, the measurement noise covariance, $R$, is inflated via a two-layer gate: a sigmoid envelope keyed to the signal $C/N_0$, modulated by a dynamics indicator derived from the discriminator output statistics of the Loop Bandwidth Control Algorithm. During noise-dominated periods the gate inflates~$R$, reducing the Kalman gain so the filter coasts on the navigation-aided prediction; when dynamics are detected the gate opens within one epoch, restoring the high-bandwidth tuning. The navigation aiding is formulated as a stochastic control input whose uncertainty is propagated from the navigation EKF covariance. Simulation results on a 20\,g acceleration step scenario show that the adapted vector architecture doubles the lock-retention rate relative to the standalone scalar filter at $C/N_0 = 31$\,dB-Hz. The receiver is implemented in MSGR, an open-source MATLAB GNSS software-defined receiver.

nominations.title: Group Physical-Layer Authentication and Confidential Beamforming in Non-Terrestrial Networks
nominations.authors: Parsa Rajabi, Mohammad Reza Abedi, Paeiz Azmi, Nader Mokari
nominations.abstract: Coordinated high-altitude platform station (HAPS) networks need to authenticate group responses and protect private data under shared power constraints. This paper studies joint group physical-layer authentication (PLA) and confidential beamforming using a fresh secret tag superimposed on private data. For received attacks independent of the current tag, we derive exact finite-block expressions for false acceptance and legitimate rejection. These expressions translate authentication error targets into a required tag signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR). We establish a nonzero asymptotic tag-energy floor and analyze residual frequency offset and peak-power restrictions. The legitimate receiver removes the tag by orthogonal projection, which discards one temporal dimension. For colluding eavesdroppers, we identify the spatial coverage condition under which artificial noise (AN) keeps their SINR bounded as data and AN powers increase together. We jointly optimize the private beams, tag beam, and AN covariance to minimize transmit power under authentication, secrecy, and per-HAPS power constraints. The method combines semidefinite relaxation (SDR), exact private-beam rank reduction, and feasible successive convex approximation. A corrected dual lower bound measures the remaining optimality gap. Numerical results show that increasing the tag length from 16 to 64 symbols reduces the required tag SINR by 7.16 dB. Joint beam design reduces mean transmit power by 27.4% relative to an optimized fixed-tag-direction baseline. The authentication guarantee requires fresh secret tags and excludes relays of the current response.

nominations.title: Learning Joint Synchronization, Channel Estimation, and Decoding: Comparison with a Finite-Blocklength Achievability Bound
nominations.authors: Bingcheng Chen, Giuseppe Durisi, Christian H\"ager
nominations.abstract: Learned schemes that jointly perform tasks such as synchronization and decoding have achieved promising results for short-packet communication. However, it remains unclear how close their performance is to information-theoretic bounds. To investigate this question, we extend the turbo autoencoder (TurboAE) proposed in D\"orner et al. (2023) to a single-input single-output waveform channel with an unknown delay and memoryless block fading, for which an achievability bound from finite-blocklength information theory is available. Our extension incorporates a pilot-free, model-guided neural synchronizer and enables joint synchronization, channel estimation, and decoding. At a blocklength of $64$ complex symbols and a rate of one bit per channel use, the proposed TurboAE achieves a lower bit error rate (BER) than all evaluated pilot-assisted 5G baselines, with gains of $1.9$ dB at a BER of $10^{-3}$ over a baseline involving a low-density parity-check (LDPC) code and $1.7$ dB over a baseline involving a polar code and successive cancellation list decoding (list size $8$). In terms of block error rate (BLER), the TurboAE outperforms the LDPC-coded baseline, but lags behind the polar-coded baseline by about $0.8$ dB at a BLER of $10^{-3}$. Moreover, all evaluated schemes remain at least $2.1$ dB away from a pilot-assisted achievability bound, indicating substantial room for improved designs.

nominations.title: Dynamic-Aware LC-DMA Beam Tracking for LEO Satellite Communications
nominations.authors: Mohamadreza Delbari, Mohammad Zarei, Denis Giniatoulline, Vahid Jamali
nominations.abstract: Liquid crystal (LC)-based dynamic metasurface antennas (DMAs) offer a power-efficient, low-cost, and scalable solution for low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communications where large apertures are needed to compensate for large path loss in the Earth-satellite link. However, beam tracking with LC-DMAs is governed by two coupled dynamics: the required time-varying beam direction caused by user and satellite mobility, and the finite response time of the LC phase shifters. This raises the question of whether LC-DMAs can reconfigure sufficiently fast to support high-mobility LEO satellite links. To address this problem, we develop a dynamic-aware beam-tracking framework that explicitly accounts for both dynamics. In particular, we formulate an optimization problem to maximize the cumulative received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) over a predictive tracking horizon subject to the physical dynamics of the LC unit cells as well as transmit power constraints. To solve this non-convex problem efficiently, we develop an alternating optimization framework combining a closed-form maximum ratio transmission (MRT) digital precoder and maximum ratio combining (MRC) with a parallel, closed-form dynamic-aware phase-shift update. Simulation results show that when the time response of LC-DMAs is properly accounted for, it can support practical mobility scenarios. Moreover, the proposed dynamic-aware algorithm maintains stable SNR and outperforms conventional designs, particularly at high vehicle velocities and low orbital azimuth angles.

nominations.title: Limitation of Bessel Beams in Near Field Communications: A Depth of Field Perspective
nominations.authors: Aditya Jolly, Vitaly Petrov, G\'abor Fodor, Emil Bj\"ornson
nominations.abstract: Bessel beams have recently been explored as a candidate complement to focused beams in radiative near-field communications due to their non-diffracting and self-healing properties. However, recent work has shown that the practically useful range of finite-aperture Bessel beams can occupy only a fraction of the radiative near-field region, establishing the existence of a finite propagation limit. In this paper, we establish such a limitation analytically from a depth-of-field perspective for Bessel beams generated by finite circular and square apertures. To quantify the Bessel beam depth, we first derive analytical expressions for the normalized array gain and use them to establish absolute and peak-normalized $3$-dB depth-of-field criteria. These criteria reveal critical cone-angle thresholds that partition the Bessel-beam configuration space into (i) undefined, (ii) finite, and (iii) infinite depth-of-field regimes. Our analysis further reveals that the maximum usable non-diffracting range under the proposed depth-of-field criterion is limited to $\approx22\%$ and $\approx19\%$ of the Fraunhofer distance for circular and square apertures, respectively. Numerical results confirm the accuracy of the derived limits for discrete planar arrays, providing practical engineering guidelines for the design of finite-aperture Bessel beams in future near-field communications.

nominations.title: RFLocMatch: Reference-Conditioned Residual Learning from Angle-Delay Spectra for Accurate Localization
nominations.authors: Leihao Zhao, Xiucheng Wang, Junxi Huang, Conghao Zhou, Yuxiang Zhang, Huixin Xu, Nan Cheng
nominations.abstract: Radio fingerprint localization supports mobile robots and location-aware services when satellite positioning is unreliable. Angle-delay power fingerprints capture power distributions over angles and delays, but localization remains vulnerable to spatial ambiguity and measurement perturbations. Reflections and blockage can produce similar fingerprints at distant locations, while noise in query fingerprints can alter query-reference rankings despite a clean reference library. These effects can place a distant reference first in the ranking, creating tail errors. Similarity scores can generate plausible candidates, but reliable selection requires candidate-specific residual evidence and comparison across alternatives. This separation motivates RFLocMatch, which uses complementary joint and link-specific matching to preserve candidate locations supported by different links. Reference-conditioned residual learning then scores each candidate using the query and reference fingerprints, their absolute difference, and their element-wise product, while candidate-context modeling compares alternatives. Tail-focused training emphasizes costly errors, and inference replaces the initial match only when a candidate's score advantage exceeds a validation-calibrated threshold. On ray-tracing-generated data, RFLocMatch reduces dual-transmitter 99th-percentile error by 75.2% under link and receiver perturbations relative to the best-performing baseline. On real-world single-transmitter channel impulse response (CIR) measurements with motion-assisted angular-spectrum estimation, it attains 8.25-m 90th-percentile error and 3.83-m mean absolute error.

nominations.title: RSS-Based Verification of Drone Remote ID Position Claims with Unknown Transmit Power
nominations.authors: Cole Dickerson, Ismail Guvenc, Wahab Khawaja, Ali Cafer Gurbuz
nominations.abstract: Broadcast Remote Identification (Remote ID) is a key enabler for integrating unmanned aircraft into the airspace. However, the position it reports is self-declared and can be falsified with low-cost hardware. In this paper, we study how Remote ID receivers can verify the declared position from the received signal strength (RSS) when neither the transmit power nor the path-loss exponent is known. In particular, we derive a Rao score test whose null distribution is exactly chi-squared for any number of packets. Its threshold and detection probability therefore follow in closed form. We then bound the detection probability of any detector that is invariant to the unknown link parameters. This bound saturates as the falsified position recedes along a fixed bearing, so a sufficiently large falsification can remain undetectable. From this limit, we obtain the worst-case bearing in closed form, the observation length needed to close it, and a receiver placement rule. Simulation results show that the proposed test considerably outperforms an estimate-then-threshold detector at low false-alarm rates.

nominations.title: RadioTraj3D: Height-Aware Adaptive Sampling for 3D Radio-Map Reconstruction from Ultra-Sparse Trajectories
nominations.authors: Zixuan Guo, Xiucheng Wang, Wenshuo Chen, Conghao Zhou, Chuan Huang, Ruijin Sun, Nan Cheng
nominations.abstract: Aerial networks require radio propagation information at unvisited positions and heights to plan routes, select links, and allocate wireless resources. A three-dimensional radio map (3D RM) represents propagation conditions over the service area, enabling these decisions before flight. However, constructing such a map from autonomous aerial vehicle (AAV) measurements is challenging, since radio measurements are available only along the trajectory, whereas the target covers the 3D service volume. Existing methods use fixed AAV trajectories that ignore how building distributions and heights affect electromagnetic propagation, missing the heights most informative for RM reconstruction. To address these issues, we propose RadioTraj3D, which uses building-height information to coordinate measurement selection and layer-wise reconstruction. Building-height variations reveal propagation-sensitive layers that guide height-adaptive sampling. We therefore propose G-METS to select geometry-sensitive heights and allocate an exact budget across edge, corridor, and open regions before channel acquisition. A dual-view reconstructor then integrates local three-dimensional boundaries with full-height context through one bounded coefficient per layer. Simulated outdoor and indoor maps demonstrate state-of-the-art reconstruction across environments and vertical grids. On real-world AAV measurements from the LACN dataset, RadioTraj3D improves peak signal-to-noise ratio by 0.84 dB and reduces normalized mean squared error by 17.5% over Completion AE.

nominations.title: Improving Spectral Resolution via Simultaneous Extracochlear and Apical Ground Contacts: A Neural Simulation Study
nominations.authors: Jared A. Rybarczyk, Erin L. Bratu, Robert F. Labadie, Jack H. Noble
nominations.abstract: Objectives: While cochlear implants (CI) can provide excellent speech perception outcomes, speech recognition in noise remains a consistent problem for many patients due to channel interaction. Recent work shows the clinical feasibility of an apical return contact placed in the cochlear helicotrema, which presents new possibilities in terms of experimental stimulation schemes. This study explores the interactions between apical and extracochlear ground contacts, aiming to characterize the effects of dual ground usage on auditory nerve fiber (ANF) dynamics and determine their utility in improving spectral resolution. Design: 6 patients with CIs were used in this retrospective study. Volume conduction models encompassing patient specific electro-anatomical characteristics and ANF compartment models defining neural dynamics were used to generate activation thresholds for 75 evenly spaced fiber bundles throughout each modeled cochlea and for 4 different grounding configurations, including the use of combined grounds. We compare our intra-patient models in terms of threshold shifts and standard deviation of fiber proportions to determine the effects of ground configuration used on channel interaction. Results: For all 6 patients, we observe shifts in ANF activation thresholds for the combined ground models indicative of more specific fiber stimulation per contact. Additionally, our combined ground models exhibit reduced fiber proportion standard deviation for several contacts of the stimulating array when compared to the standard extracochlear ground configuration or apical ground configuration. Conclusions: The shifts in activation thresholds and reduction in standard deviations suggest that stimulation schemes utilizing extracochlear and apical grounds in conjunction can provide reduced channel interaction and enhanced spectral resolution for certain contacts in an array.

nominations.title: B-ExposNet: Bayesian Deep Learning for EMF Exposure Mapping with Uncertainty Quantification
nominations.authors: Yukun Liu, Shanshan Wang, Paul Lagouanelle, Yarui Zhang, Joe Wiart
nominations.abstract: Electromagnetic field exposure in urban environments is highly variable, and conventional exposure maps provide a deterministic estimate, without considering its uncertainty. To address the gap, this paper proposes B-ExposNet, a Bayesian neural network for spatial exposure estimation with uncertainty quantification. B-ExposNet extends ExposNet by treating the weights of regression head as random variables, inferred by variational inference, so that the model provides probabilistic estimates from posterior predictive distribution. The method is evaluated on drive-test measurement campaigns conducted in three French cities, and compared with conventional method such as universal Kriging, in both predictive accuracy and the quality of the estimated uncertainty. On the test region, B-ExposNet achieves a mean absolute percentage error of 28.19\% and a continuous ranked probability score of 0.198~V/m, improving on canonical methods in both accuracy and uncertainty quantification.

nominations.title: Grid-Refinement SBL for AFDM Channel Estimation Under Fractional Delay and Fractional Doppler Channels
nominations.authors: Qu Luo, Limin Liu, Zhe Li, Qihao Peng, Haowei Wu, Pei Xiao
nominations.abstract: This paper investigates channel estimation for affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) systems over channels with fractional delay and fractional Doppler (FDFD) shifts. An exact FDFD channel model is first established, and the corresponding input--output relationship is also derived. To address the FDFD-induced delay--Doppler coupling, a first-order linear approximation grid-refinement sparse Bayesian learning (FLA-GR-SBL) method is developed. To further remedy the convergence and stability issues caused by the limited accuracy of the first-order approximation, we propose a two-dimensional grid-approximation SBL (2D-GA-SBL) algorithm, which iteratively refines the delay--Doppler grid and thereby characterizes the channel more accurately. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithms significantly outperform existing on-grid and off-grid SBL benchmarks in terms of both normalized mean square error (NMSE) and bit error rate (BER).

nominations.title: Embodied Movable Antennas
nominations.authors: Yewen Cao, Dengke Wei, Yulin Shao
nominations.abstract: This paper introduces embodied movable antennas (MAs), a new MA architecture that rethinks the source of antenna mobility. Unlike conventional MAs that rely on dedicated antenna actuators, embodied MAs harness the mechanical degrees of freedom already present in physical agents to reconfigure antenna position and orientation. We distinguish two modes of embodied MAs: task-coupled and task-preserving. Focusing on the latter, we show how wireless channels can be reconfigured by exploiting task-equivalent host configurations without altering the prescribed physical task. Using a redundant robotic manipulator as a canonical realization, we characterize the intrinsically coupled antenna translation and orientation induced by task-preserving self-motion and derive an exact Fourier representation of the resulting multipath channel. Our analysis reveals that the wireless value of embodied mobility depends not merely on how far an antenna can move, but on which configurations remain feasible under the physical task and how their coupled motion interacts with polarization and multipath propagation. Building on this insight, we develop a cross-task antenna mounting design that enables wireless adaptation with a fixed physical installation. Numerical results demonstrate substantial communication gains through task-preserving motion. These findings establish mechanical redundancy as a new, quantifiable resource for wireless channel reconfiguration.

nominations.title: Finite-Element Electromagnetic Analysis and Evaluation of Antenna Performance Metrics Using a Quantum Linear System Solver
nominations.authors: Hiroaki Ominato, Takahiro Ohyama, Shiro Kawabata
nominations.abstract: Electromagnetic analysis based on the finite element method is widely used in antenna design. At higher frequencies, however, the required mesh refinement makes solving large sparse linear systems the main contributor to computational cost. Quantum linear system solvers offer a potential means of accelerating this step, but their output is a superposition state: reconstructing all components of the classical solution vector would forfeit the quantum speedup. Prior studies have proposed methods for obtaining physical quantities such as scattering cross sections and scattering parameters from the solution state. To support antenna design using fault-tolerant quantum computers, we formulate the total radiated power, the radiated power within a prescribed solid angle, and the dielectric and conductive losses as observables for efficient evaluation from a quantum solution state. These observables avoid the measurement cost of reconstructing all components of the output quantum state. We develop an end-to-end hybrid quantum--classical workflow that combines finite-element electromagnetic analysis, matrix preconditioning, a quantum linear system solver, and the evaluation of antenna design metrics. To validate the workflow, we performed numerical experiments evaluating these observables for an axisymmetric coaxially fed monopole antenna. Under idealized conditions, the relative errors in the total radiated power and the dissipated power with respect to the classical finite-element solution were on the order of $10^{-3}$, confirming the consistency of the workflow. The proposed method is expected to provide a basis for using quantum linear system solvers to evaluate antenna performance and, in the future, to design high-frequency wireless devices.

nominations.title: Finite-resource cooling of qudits beyond thermodynamic length
nominations.authors: Ansh Mishra, Aryan Senthilkumar
nominations.abstract: Cooling a quantum system with $N$ thermal machines costs more than Landauer's bound. For swap-based collision models the excess is set by thermodynamic length, which is optimal for qubits and was suggested by numerics to be optimal in general. We show that for qudits, permutations of energy eigenstates that use several resonant transitions at once do better for every spectrum, reducing the excess by up to 83% near the ground state. To second order, coherent collisions do no better, and at infinite temperature $d_M$-level machines reduce the excess by at most a factor $d_M-1$.

nominations.title: Quantum manifestations of converse symmetry breaking
nominations.authors: Daniel P. Buser, Biswabibek Bandyopadhyay, Adilson E. Motter
nominations.abstract: Quantum synchronization holds promise in advancing quantum technologies such as sensing, communication, and computation. A key challenge in this rapidly developing field is to identify mechanisms that can promote the emergence of synchronous dynamics. Here, we show that quantum synchronization can be enhanced by introducing controlled heterogeneity in the form of coupling mismatches. Using spin van der Pol oscillators as a model system, we show that this mechanism constitutes a quantum analog of the phenomenon of converse symmetry breaking previously identified in classical oscillator networks, where a synchronous state is stabilized by explicit symmetry breaking.
